title: An Efficient Method for Immortalizing Mouse Embryonic Fibroblasts by CRISPR-mediated Deletion of the Tp53 Gene
author: Srisathya Srinivasan

steps.title: Prepare 0.1% trypsin solution
steps.instruction: Mix 40 mg trypsin from bovine pancreas with 40 mL HBSS (1×), filter‑sterilize through a 0.22 µm syringe filter, aliquot, snap‑freeze in liquid nitrogen and store at –80 °C.

steps.title: Prepare complete cell culture media
steps.instruction: Combine 500 mL DMEM (high glucose, 1×) with 50 mL FBS (10 %), 5.5 mL Penicillin‑Streptomycin (100×, 1×), and 5.5 mL L‑glutamine (200 mM, 2 mM final). Filter‑sterilize (0.22 µm), pre‑warm at 37 °C before use. For freshly isolated MEFs add sodium pyruvate (1 mM final, 100 µL) and MEM NEAA (1× final, 100 µL) per 10 mL; for post‑electroporation use media without Pen‑Strep.

steps.title: Prepare cell freezing media
steps.instruction: Mix 45 mL complete culture media (90 %) with 5 mL DMSO (10 %). Filter‑sterilize (0.22 µm) and keep on ice.

steps.title: Set up timed mating
steps.instruction: Place male and female mice together, check females each morning for vaginal plugs; separate plugged females and house them alone until 12.5 days post‑coitum.

steps.title: Euthanize dam and dissect embryos
steps.instruction: Euthanize the pregnant dam at 12.5 dpc by CO₂ inhalation followed by cervical dislocation, spray abdomen with 70 % ethanol, dissect uterine horns, rinse in PBS in a 100 mm dish, and keep horns on ice.

steps.title: Isolate individual embryos
steps.instruction: Place each embryo in a 60 mm dish containing HBSS, under a dissecting microscope remove placenta and embryonic sac (rinse sac briefly in deionized water), discard brain, eyes and internal organs, then transfer each embryo to a separate well of a 6‑well plate filled with HBSS kept on ice.

steps.title: Label tubes for homogenization
steps.instruction: Label one 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube per embryo.

steps.title: Add DNase and trypsin to tubes
steps.instruction: To each labeled tube add 25 µL RQ1 DNase (1 U/µL) and 0.5 mL 0.1 % trypsin, mix 2–3 times with a P1000 pipette.

steps.title: Homogenize embryos
steps.instruction: Transfer one embryo (still in HBSS) into its tube, pipette up/down 12–15 times with a P1000 until tissue is in small chunks (avoid over‑homogenization; viscosity indicates over‑lysis). Keep tube on ice and repeat for all embryos.

steps.title: Incubate homogenates with trypsin
steps.instruction: Place tubes on a pre‑warmed metal rack (37 °C) and incubate exactly 8 min, inverting each tube about every 3 min to mix.

steps.title: Prepare cold neutralization media
steps.instruction: For each embryo, add 5 mL cold complete culture media (supplemented with sodium pyruvate and MEM NEAA as above) to a 50 mL conical tube; keep tubes on ice.

steps.title: Neutralize trypsin
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL of the cold media from step 9 to each homogenate tube, mix gently 2–3 times with a P1000, then transfer the entire 5 mL mixture into the corresponding 50 mL tube containing the remaining 4 mL cold media.

steps.title: Gentle mixing of cell suspension
steps.instruction: Using a 5 mL serological pipette, pipette the mixture up/down 8–10 times very gently.

steps.title: Centrifuge cell suspensions
steps.instruction: Spin at 500 × g for 10 min at room temperature in a swinging‑bucket rotor.

steps.title: Prepare pre‑warmed culture dishes
steps.instruction: For each embryo, add 10 mL pre‑warmed complete media to a 100 mm TC‑treated dish and supplement with 100 µL sodium pyruvate (1 mM final) and 100 µL MEM NEAA (1× final). Keep dishes in the incubator (37 °C, 5 % CO₂, 90–95 % humidity).

steps.title: Resuspend cell pellets
steps.instruction: Aspirate supernatant carefully without disturbing the pellet, gently resuspend each pellet in 1 mL of the supplemented media from step 13, and transfer the suspension back to its corresponding pre‑warmed 100 mm dish.

steps.title: Incubate primary MEFs overnight
steps.instruction: Shake plates gently for even distribution and incubate undisturbed at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂, 90–95 % humidity until the next morning.

steps.title: Assess confluence next morning
steps.instruction: Check that cultures are ~80 % confluent (full confluence in 2–3 days). Note that tissue clumps may remain; leave them untouched.

steps.title: Passage or freeze MEFs
steps.instruction: Wash each 100 mm dish once with sterile PBS, add 3.5 mL pre‑warmed 0.25 % trypsin‑EDTA, incubate 1–2 min until cells detach, neutralize with 7 mL complete media, filter through a 40 µm cell strainer into a 50 mL tube, centrifuge 500 × g for 5 min at RT, aspirate supernatant.

steps.title: Culture split of MEFs
steps.instruction: Resuspend pellet in 1 mL complete media, pipette 12–15 times with a P1000, and split into new dishes (ideally ≤1:5 split).

steps.title: Freeze MEFs for storage
steps.instruction: Resuspend pellet in 1 mL cell freezing media, aliquot into cryogenic vials, place vials in a room‑temperature Mr. Frosty container, transfer to –80 °C overnight, then move to liquid nitrogen for long‑term storage. Use eye protection, cryo‑gloves and lab coat when handling liquid nitrogen.

steps.title: Seed MEFs for immortalization
steps.instruction: Two days before electroporation, seed MEFs (passage 0 or 1) so they reach 70–90 % confluence on the day of electroporation; aim for 200 k–2 M cells (typically 1–2 million cells in two wells of a 6‑well plate).

steps.title: Prepare plasmids at 1 µg/µL
steps.instruction: Adjust concentrations of Px461‑Cas9n‑Trp53‑sgRNA‑alpha (Addgene 88846), Px461‑Cas9n‑Trp53‑sgRNA‑beta (Addgene 88847), and pCAG‑GFP (Addgene 11150) to 1 µg/µL.

steps.title: Pre‑warm electroporation supplies
steps.instruction: In a biosafety cabinet, pre‑warm a 24‑well plate with 500 µL culture media lacking penicillin‑streptomycin per well and pre‑warm 0.25 % trypsin‑EDTA.

steps.title: Harvest cells for electroporation
steps.instruction: Wash cells once with 1 mL PBS per 6‑well, add 0.3 mL 0.25 % trypsin‑EDTA, incubate 1–2 min at 37 °C until cells lift, neutralize with 0.7 mL media without pen‑strept (per well), transfer suspension to a 1.5 mL tube.

steps.title: Generate single‑cell suspension
steps.instruction: Pipette the cell mixture 8–10 times with a P1000, then count cells while still in trypsin/media.

steps.title: Aliquot cells for CRISPR and GFP
steps.instruction: Dispense 100 000 cells into each of two 1.5 mL tubes (each electroporation will use 50 000 cells; double the amount to allow for pipetting loss).

steps.title: Wash cells before transfection
steps.instruction: Centrifuge tubes at 500 × g for 5 min, aspirate supernatant, resuspend pellet in 0.5 mL PBS, centrifuge again, aspirate PBS completely.

steps.title: Add TransIT‑LT1 to cell pellets
steps.instruction: Resuspend each pellet in 20 µL TransIT‑LT1 (gives 5 × 10⁶ cells · mL⁻¹). Remove as much residual PBS as possible before adding the reagent.

steps.title: Prepare DNA‑cell reaction mixtures
steps.instruction: For the CRISPR mixture add 0.5 µL Px461‑alpha plasmid and 0.25 µL Px461‑beta plasmid to the 20 µL cell‑TransIT suspension; for the GFP control add 1 µL pCAG‑GFP. Mix gently with a P20 pipette (final volume ≈20 µL).

steps.title: Load Neon electroporator
steps.instruction: Fill a Neon electroporation tube with 3 mL buffer E, place the tube in the Neon pipette station inside the biosafety cabinet, and attach a Neon tip by pressing the push‑button to the second stop and inserting the tip firmly.

steps.title: Electroporate CRISPR cells
steps.instruction: Pipette 10 µL of the CRISPR reaction mixture into the Neon tip (avoid air bubbles, ensure uniform suspension), insert tip into the buffer E‑filled tube, and electroporate using 1350 V, 30 ms, 1 pulse. Immediately dispense the cells into a pre‑warmed well of the 24‑well plate (500 µL media). Gently shake the plate for even distribution.

steps.title: Electroporate GFP control cells
steps.instruction: Repeat the loading, electroporation (same parameters) and transfer steps with the GFP reaction mixture. One Neon tip may be reused up to six times, but a fresh tip can be used if desired.

steps.title: Post‑electroporation incubation
steps.instruction: Place the 24‑well plate in a 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ incubator (90–95 % humidity). Observe cell viability ~2 h later; keep plate disturbance to a minimum.

steps.title: Assess GFP expression
steps.instruction: At 16–24 h post‑electroporation, examine the GFP control wells under an inverted fluorescence microscope; expect >30 % of healthy cells to be GFP‑positive (20–60 % overall cell death is typical).

steps.title: Replace media with complete media
steps.instruction: 16–24 h after electroporation, change the culture media in each well to complete cell culture media (contains penicillin‑streptomycin).

steps.title: Expand and passage immortalized MEFs
steps.instruction: Continue culturing, splitting at ~1:15 when confluent, until GFP‑control cells die (usually 2–3 weeks). Tp53‑CRISPR cells should proliferate robustly, indicating successful immortalization.

steps.title: Freeze established iMEFs
steps.instruction: Harvest immortalized MEFs as in step 19, resuspend in cell freezing media, aliquot into cryogenic vials, place in Mr. Frosty at room temperature, freeze at –80 °C overnight, then transfer to liquid nitrogen for long‑term storage.
